issue.title: [Jazzy] Broken libzstd dependency on Ubuntu 24.04 (arm64/Raspberry Pi) prevents apt installation
issue.body:
### Generated by Generative AI

Gemini 3 Pro

### Operating System:

Ubuntu Server 24.04.3 LTS on Raspberry Pi 4 (arm64)

### ROS version or commit hash:

Jazzy (Binary installation via apt)

### RMW implementation (if applicable):

rmw_fastrtps_cpp (Default)

### RMW Configuration (if applicable):

_No response_

### Client library (if applicable):

rclcpp / rclpy

### 'ros2 doctor --report' output

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce issue

Set up a fresh Raspberry Pi 4 with Ubuntu Server 24.04.3 LTS (arm64).

Follow the official Jazzy installation guide:

Set locale.

Enable Ubuntu Universe.

Add the ROS 2 GPG key and repository.

Attempt to install the base packages:

Bash

sudo apt update
sudo apt install ros-jazzy-ros-base

### Expected behavior

The command should resolve all dependencies and install ros-jazzy-ros-base successfully, as Ubuntu 24.04 is a Tier 1 supported platform for Jazzy.

### Actual behavior

The installation fails with an "impossible situation" error due to a version mismatch for libzstd:

Plaintext

The following packages have unmet dependencies:
 libzstd-dev : Depends: libzstd1 (= 1.5.5+dfsg2-2build1) but 1.5.5+dfsg2-2build1.1 is to be installed
 ros-jazzy-rcl : Depends: ros-jazzy-tracetools but it is not installable
 E: Unable to correct problems, you have held broken packages.
The system has 1.5.5+dfsg2-2build1.1 (from Ubuntu updates), but the ROS 2 Jazzy binaries are strictly pinned to the older 1.5.5+dfsg2-2build1 version.

### Additional information

This issue effectively breaks the "Tier 1" promise for Raspberry Pi users on the latest Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS. A manual downgrade of libzstd1 is required as a workaround, but this is not user-friendly and may conflict with other system security updates.

The binary packages in the ROS repository need to be re-synced or rebuilt against the updated libzstd version found in the current noble-updates repository.
